summary: Kabambare territory (Maniema) is mostly state-administered in its western Lusangi secteur and around Kabambare centre and Wamaza, with police the main day-to-day authority. The Salamabila secteur in the north-east is the stronghold of Mai-Mai Malaika, which has fought the FARDC around Salamabila town and the Namoya gold mine since ~2017; the army holds the town and mine area while Malaika dominates parts of the forest hinterland. The far east toward Fizi (Lulenge/Kimbi) is a Mai-Mai/Wazalendo operating area with weak state presence. NOTE: web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, fetch domains blocked), so all zones rest on prior knowledge and are low confidence.

sources.title: UN Group of Experts on the DRC – final reports (2019–2025), sections on Mai-Mai Malaika in Salamabila and armed groups in Fizi/Kabambare
Radio Okapi – Kabambare tag (Mai-Mai Malaika incursions in Salamabila, FARDC operations, Kabambare centre)
Kivu Security Tracker – armed groups in Fizi (CNPSC/Yakutumba, Mai-Mai coalitions) bordering Kabambare

zones.description: Salamabila town (Kitoko, Lubinga, Akilibangi, Kimputu, Kopakopa, Matchapano) and the Namoya gold-mine area (Matete), Saramabila health zone
zones.evidence: Salamabila centre and the Namoya mine concession have had a permanent FARDC deployment since Mai-Mai Malaika (Sheikh Hassan) began attacking the Banro-operated mine around 2017-2019; Malaika has repeatedly raided the town outskirts and mining camps. Assessment from background knowledge of UN GoE and Radio Okapi reporting; web research tools were unavailable, so no 2026 confirmation.

zones.description: Rural central/eastern Salamabila secteur (Kayembe, Kihonya, Amusini, Salumu-Basikibunda, Agenda) and Tengetenge villages of Lusangi health zone
zones.evidence: Mai-Mai Malaika is based in the forested hinterland of Salamabila secteur, taxing artisanal gold sites and villages and periodically clashing with FARDC. Exact village-level control is not documented; assigned by proximity to Malaika's known area of operation. No source could be fetched for this run.

zones.description: Western Salamabila secteur around Wamaza (Mutakuya/Wamaza, Kiviluka, Kawaya, Mulozi, Kingombe, Mwangundu, Mayembe)
zones.evidence: Wamaza is a large gold-mining town with state administration, police and FARDC posts; Malaika activity is reported mainly further east around Salamabila/Namoya. Default state presence with possible Malaika incursions.

zones.description: Lusangi secteur (Lukoma/Lusangi, Muzingandu, Nyezi, Muyombo, Kasesa, Ayuza, Kavima) toward Kasongo and Kongolo
zones.evidence: No significant armed-group control reported for Lusangi secteur; state administration and police posts assumed in the main villages.

zones.description: Kabambare secteur, centre and west (Kabambare centre/Mbundu, Sombe, Lubambi, Mwanamwamba, Katemema, Kazabu, Shabimba, Kiyanga)
zones.evidence: Kabambare centre is the territorial administrative seat with police and an FARDC presence; no reports of armed-group control of the town or its western hinterland were found in prior knowledge.

zones.description: Eastern Kabambare toward the Fizi border and Kimbi-Lulenge health zone (Lwandiko, Mahembe, Kagulwe, Kabeya, Kahoho, Babinza, Matama, Bulungu, Mkungandala, Mukosamali)
zones.evidence: The forested Lulenge/Kimbi area straddling the Fizi-Kabambare border is a long-standing operating area of Mai-Mai groups (CNPSC/Yakutumba and allied factions, now largely aligned with Wazalendo) with limited state presence; the specific controlling faction per village is unknown.
